set.approach: From the lower Jungle parking, drive on to the meadow, turn left into it and follow the two-track to the parking at the top of the valley. Walk the old logging road left of a fence southeast through a short stretch of dense deadfall, take the first break on the left (small cairn), and follow it to a primitive trail on the right that leads to the cliff's edge. A cairned trail runs southeast to the crag, with the north entrance marked by two cairns. The route starts in the big red corner.

The route is a short way right of the Mini (Little) Mesa, the next line right of the face corner and just left of the chimney.

From the lower Jungle parking, drive on to the meadow, turn left into it and follow the two-track to the parking at the top of the valley. Walk the old logging road left of a fence southeast through a short stretch of dense deadfall, take the first break on the left (small cairn), and follow it to a primitive trail on the right that leads to the cliff's edge. A cairned trail runs southeast to the crag, with the north entrance marked by two cairns. From the south entrance, walk the long cliff for a short way to the obvious crack line with wedged blocks.

Past Mount DeMoisy at Snowbasin's south end, the Hogs Back is a rib made of stacked low-angle slabs. Reach it from the gondola or the Needles Lodge by following the road south toward the DeMoisy chairlift, then the road past the top of the Strawberry gondola, which turns north and then south again to the base of the formation. The route begins where the Hogs Back is lowest and runs up its middle.

The Sisters are reached from the Snowbasin gondola by walking up to the DeMoisy chairlift's top terminal and carrying on south on the road to a sharper turn, where talus begins. At the talus turn left and drop to the lowest face of the Sisters; a bit of bushwhacking and scree gets you to the foot of the route.

Leave the car at the Bald Mountain trailhead and hike the Notch Mountain trail up to Notch Lake. Swing north around the lake, then push northwest through the trees to a talus field, which leads to the foot of the buttress's east side. The route is on the higher tier a short way to the right of Hall of the Mountain King, below a giant triangular roof with a zigzagging flake about two-thirds of the way up; a carved plaque set at the bottom shows where to begin.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route, using the rappel station above the trees as well.

review.notes: Route page: location and rappel. Count and rope length left out.

set.approach: Leave the car at the Bald Mountain trailhead and hike the Notch Mountain trail up to Notch Lake. Swing north around the lake, then push northwest through the trees to a talus field, which leads to the foot of the buttress's east side. The route starts a short way left of the access pitch used by the other three routes on the central column, at a bolt on a chossy pedestal.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the bolted belays, which are equipped for it; pull the ropes slowly, since they can dislodge loose rock.

review.notes: Route page: start and rappels from bolted belays.

set.approach: Leave the car at the Bald Mountain trailhead and hike the Notch Mountain trail up to Notch Lake. Swing north around the lake, then push northwest through the trees to a talus field, which leads to the foot of the buttress's east side. The route is the direct line up the middle of the buttress; once above the talus, traverse right along the cliff's foot to locate the approach pitch.
set.descent_text: Rappel from the anchor at the summit down to the midway ledge, take off the rope, and scramble climber's left over class II-III ground toward The Notch. Reach a gully running perpendicular to the notch, work down it until a ledge system on its right side doglegs right into the notch, then go down the talus and contour back to the foot of the route.

review.notes: Route page: location and full descent.

set.descent_text: Rappel the route on the bolted belays back to your packs. Take care on the top rappel, which needs attention so the rope does not run over loose blocks.

set.approach: Leave the car at the Bald Mountain trailhead and hike the Notch Mountain trail up to Notch Lake. Swing north around the lake, then push northwest through the trees to a talus field, which leads to the foot of the buttress's east side. The route starts at the same place as Hall of the Mountain King, but wanders up the blocky wide break on the left side of the bolted slab and its roof.

review.notes: No descent stated on this route page.

set.approach: Upper Jungle is the pair of cliff bands, east and west facing, on the road above the Lower Jungle parking. Park on the right, continue around the corner up the road to the marked Upper Jungle, and follow the short, cairned approach down to the crag. The route starts up a thin crack to the right of Great Ape Escape and Goodall Times.

The tier is reached from the Trial Lake area: cross the dam on the west side and follow the trail along the lake to Wall Lake, or use the Wall Lake trailhead near Crystal Lake. Work around the lake's left side beyond the main lower tier, then cross a meadow to the upper tier. The route is right of Upside Surprise, up a finger and hand crack through a roof.

Park at the top of 29th Street and hike the trail around toward the south to the first major canyon. Cross the small bridge and hike up the drainage, keeping to the trail on the north side, to the base of the climbs. Ford the creek and make your way up the blocky alcove left of Malan's Crack to a dihedral with a small tree.

Park at the top of 29th Street and hike the trail around toward the south to the first major canyon. Cross the small bridge and hike up the drainage, keeping to the trail on the north side, to the base of the climbs. It begins left of the waterfall's fall line in a right-facing dihedral, gained from a few ledges, and follows the crack system that parallels the ice route, staying dry.

Pick up the bike trail by the parking area, walk uphill, then follow the clear trail that drops to the crag. The route is reached from the top of the cliff: once the Window Crack Hole comes into view, continue southwest along the cliff top to the easiest way down on your right, then pass two short sport routes to a corner with double cracks.
set.descent_text: Once on top, build an anchor if needed and cross to the trail along the cliff top.

review.notes: Route page: location and the walk to the cliff-top trail.
